correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from first principles: costate p(t)=X sinh(q(2-t))/D solves the strictly convex scalar LQ boundary-value system and gives the true-plant transition m=e^{2a}-H/D. Independence gives exact all-p moment products. Strict convexity of (A^p+B^p)/2, the SLLN for bounded log multipliers, and independence/positivity of quadratic stage costs complete the infinite-horizon proof. Independent RK4 checks endpoints but is not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The source method optimizes a quadratic objective and measures stability using expected absolute state. A robust counterexample where absolute expectation decays but expected realized quadratic costs grow (hence total expected cost is infinite despite finite almost-sure total cost) exposes a substantive performance gap. The exact positive moment cutoff characterizes the entire risk spectrum, not merely a negative example. Strict inequalities persist under nearby drift/horizon parameters. This scalar example is not claimed to yield computation savings or a broad numerical method.
